bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO—Citi raises PT to $240, Bernstein upgrades to Outperform
bullets.body: NVIDIA's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO and board director after receiving input from senior U.S. government officials confirming no national security risk; Trump publicly backed the decision. Citi raised PT to $240 from $225 (15x FY28E EPS, reduced CEO-transition risk discount) and Bernstein upgraded from Market Perform to Outperform with $200 PT; Wolfe maintains Outperform at $200. Key overhangs remain: ongoing board/SEC accounting investigations, Megaspeed entity-list blacklisting, congressional hearings (Jensen scheduled before Senate Banking Dec 3 and three House committees Dec 1-2), and BIS chip-export controls halting server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. NVDA surged 31.5% on the week but pared gains mid-week.

bullets.title: NVDA export-control tightening: SE Asia shipments halted; GPU resellers flood market; CoreWeave bonds at record lows
bullets.body: BIS interim final rule (effective ~Nov 19) closed the Chinese remote-access loophole for advanced Nvidia chips in third-party countries and added destination-based licensing for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil; Nvidia asked server partners (including Dell and Supermicro) to stop shipments to customers in those markets. ByteDance had deployed ~36k B200 chips in Malaysia (~$2.5B hardware cost) before the crackdown. GPU resellers flooded secondary markets with B300 chips; SpaceX cut Blackwell GPU spot rental rates 20-35% to $10-12/GPU-hour. Goldman estimated $705B AI debt YTD with CoreWeave bonds hitting record lows amid doubts over AI trade durability. Congressional backlash vowed aggressive NVDA oversight and tighter controls ahead of Jensen's Dec 3 Senate testimony.

bullets.title: DELL: Blowout Q3—$132B AI backlog, FY27 revenue guidance raised to $202B, $29.68 EPS; $25B buyback
bullets.body: Dell F3Q27 revenue $54.94B (+103% YoY) smashed consensus $49.32B; EPS $9.45 vs $6.60 consensus. AI-optimized server revenue hit $22B with $60.2B orders booked; backlog expanded to record $132.3B (+40% QoQ). FY27 guidance raised to $202B revenue (+78% YoY) and $29.68 EPS (+188% YoY); AI server revenue guidance raised to $78B (+3x). ISG operating margin 14.2% (+490bps YoY); opex fell to 7% of revenue, company record. Board approved $25B additional share repurchase. Pipeline is 'multiples of backlog.' Customer base grew ~15% QoQ to 7,500+. Despite the beat, stock initially fell ~7% as investors debated margin sustainability and CY28 DRAM pricing risk.

bullets.title: HPE: F4Q beat and raise on AI networking; FY27 guide +27-35% revenue, but Cloud/AI margins compress to ~14%
bullets.body: HPE F4Q EPS $1.43 vs $1.28 consensus; Cloud & AI revenue $11.26B (+3.6% above consensus); AI systems backlog $8.8B with networking orders +56% YoY. FY27 guidance: revenue 27-35% growth ($59.4-63.1B), EPS $5.05-5.35, FCF $5.5B+. However, Cloud & AI operating margin guided to ~16-17% in Q1 and ~14% for FY27 vs 18.4% in F4Q, sending shares down ~10-16% post-announcement. Supply constraints through H2 2028 (memory, NAND, networking components) cited. $5B added to buyback authorization (total ~$7.3B).

bullets.title: MRVL: Q3 earnings preview Dec 1—consensus $3.15B revenue, $1.10 EPS; AI connectivity upside key catalyst
bullets.body: Marvell reports Dec 1; consensus revenue $3.15B (Q4 consensus $3.74B, FY27 $12B). Bulls cite accelerating AI connectivity, custom ASIC ramp with hyperscalers (Trainium contributing now, Maia ramping), and networking >70% growth; long-term CY30 target 10x CY25 to $80B/$30 EPS. Bears flag LITE deal dilution, ambitious execution, near-term margin pressure, and NVIDIA exposure. Options imply ~15.8% move. Multiple analysts cut PTs (JPM $515→down; Opco $425→$325; RBC $250 OW) purely on group multiple compression, not thesis change. Near-term positive check: AI networking tracking above 70% growth this year.

bullets.title: SNOW: Partner checks bullish ahead of Q3 earnings Dec 1—40%+ product revenue growth expected, Cortex/CoCo driving incremental consumption
bullets.body: JPM and RBC channel work with Elite-Tier Snowflake partners shows ~20% practice growth sustained, Cortex/CoCo catching Databricks, 80-85% of pipeline tied to installed base renewals, and AI workloads now 40-45% of practice. Early CoCo adopters show ~11% incremental consumption increase. Citi cut PT to $470 from $490 (multiple compression) but reiterates Buy; expects F3Q product revenue 40%+ growth, beat vs $1.591B guidance, and FY28 guidance to frame positively vs Street's 30% consensus. Options imply ~15.8% move. Downside risk: Databricks competitive pressure and cost guardrail adoption by customers.

bullets.title: CRM: JPM reiterates OW ahead of F3Q—expects 11% organic cRPO growth, Agentforce ARR at $1.5B; PT $515
bullets.body: JPM expects F3Q organic cRPO growth ~11% (modest upside vs ~10% guide) and F4Q guide of 12%+ in CC signaling 2H re-acceleration. Agentforce ARR at $1.5B; premium mix grew to 5% of base in F2Q from 1% in F1Q25 (each 1% migration ~$100M revenue). Shares trading at 10x EV/uFCF on FY27 estimates. Wolfe cut PT to $250 from $360 on softer checks; Erste Group downgraded to Hold. Peer application software struggling with AI monetization, so CRM set up favorably on moderating expectations. Early commentary on Copilotforce (MSFT) and Claude integration monetization expected on call.

bullets.title: MDB: MongoDB earnings Dec 1—consensus $762M revenue, $1.61 EPS; Atlas growth accelerating to ~28-29% vs 26% guide
bullets.body: MongoDB reports Dec 1 at 17:00 ET. DADCO expects Atlas growth ~28-29% YoY vs 26% guidance, with EA & Other ARR showing acceleration; RBC maintains Outperform at $465 PT heading into print. Wolfe notes narrative dominated by leadership transition and M&A questions but checks turning positive with cRPO acceleration in F3Q and F4Q guide. KeyBanc previews F3Q beat potential on Atlas momentum. Options imply approximately mid-teens% move.

bullets.title: CRWD: Record Q3—27% ARR growth, 58% NNARR; acquires ZS for $43.9B all-stock (1.135x); Guggenheim upgrades to Buy
bullets.body: CrowdStrike F3Q27: revenue $1.583B (+28% YoY, beat $1.53B); NNARR $419M (+58% YoY, fifth consecutive quarter of acceleration); Falcon Guardian AI security >$100M ARR in <1 year. CRWD raised FY27 net new ARR guidance to $1.459-1.463B (+44-45% YoY). Simultaneously announced $43.9B all-stock acquisition of Zscaler (1.135 CRWD shares/ZS share = $260.41/share); targeting $1B annualized revenue synergies by 30 months post-close, $500M cost synergies in 18-24 months; deal expected to close H2 FY2028. Guggenheim upgraded CRWD to Buy at $280; multiple ZS downgrades across the Street (Jefferies, Bernstein, Macquarie, Rosenblatt all cut to Hold/Neutral). ACN cybersecurity business viewed as beneficiary of consolidation wave.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM reiterates OW at $200 PT; enterprise tracker shows acceleration with BFCM >30% GMV growth as key test
bullets.body: SHOP enterprise activity logged ~14 announcements in 3Q26 vs 10 in 2Q (36% new clients, 36% launches, 29% expansions), including luxury brands (Givenchy, Chaumet). Enterprise estimated at ~5% of 2026E revenue rising to ~7% in 2027E. BFCM 2025 showed 27% YoY GMV growth (24% ex-FX); investors expect >30% in 2026 as a 'high bar.' UCP adoption at 15.1% of Top 2,500 e-commerce sites per Piper. SHOP.CN rallied +9.6% on the AI rally week.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY OSB GGR +10% YoY week ending 11/22; DKNG weekly share +23% but 4QTD -7%; NFL holds pressuring Q4
bullets.body: NY OSB GGR +10% YoY and handle +11% YoY for week ending 11/22/26; 4QTD GGR tracking -9% YoY. DraftKings weekly GGR +23% YoY maintaining 32% market share, though 4QTD -7%. NFL Week 11 saw 9/12 favorites win (5/5 biggest favorites), consistent with a possible low-hold week for sportsbooks—UBS flags risk to DKNG Q4 guidance. Morgan Stanley downgraded DKNG to Equal-Weight on higher PM spend ramp and visibility erosion. Citi crowding data shows DKNG short interest tripled vs 3 weeks ago.

bullets.title: PINS: +12% on executive comp severance amendment—M&A signal; Microsoft advertising integration adds upside
bullets.body: Pinterest disclosed amendments to executive change-of-control severance provisions for CEO and CLO, triggering a ~12% move. RBC views amended comp protections as raising sale odds, with potential acquirers including SHOP, AMZN, MSFT, ETSY, or PE. Separately, PINS announced a Microsoft Advertising integration giving access to search budgets. RBC sees capped UCAN MAU growth and volatile customer mix as limitations, noting upside only if compute efficiency gains show up in self-serve business or structural ad performance improvement materializes.

bullets.title: PLTR: $300M Poland defense AI deal signed; stock +3% on Friday premarket
bullets.body: Palantir signed a $300M defense AI deal with Poland, confirmed in premarket trading Friday Nov 27. PLTR had been down significantly prior to the AI rally week; the deal reinforces the government/defense AI monetization narrative that underpins the bull thesis.

bullets.title: HUBS: Argus downgrades to Hold on valuation; JPM Neutral on 'refounding' headless strategy sacrificing near-term monetization
bullets.body: Argus Research downgraded HubSpot to Hold from Buy at $210.21, citing valuation concerns. JPM maintains Neutral, noting co-founder Halligan returned as CEO on 11/12 pursuing a 'refounding' via headless pricing (MCP included at all seat levels) that prioritizes share gain over near-term monetization and investor visibility. Key stabilization signal would be net-new customer adds returning above 5K (vs F4Q guidance of sub-5K). CRSD pricing pilot has no firm timeline for scaled expansion.

bullets.title: WDAY: F3Q beat but F4Q subscription revenue guide misses; FY28 11% growth target questioned
bullets.body: Workday F3Q subscription revenue $2.53B (+12.8% YoY, slight beat); EPS $2.82 vs $2.74 consensus. AI ARR reached $750M+ (+130% YoY) with $150M new ACV. However, F4Q subscription guide of $2.600B (+10.2% YoY) missed consensus by ~$8M, and cRPO guided 10-11% (below prior 11-12% trajectory). FY28 target of ~11% subscription growth reiterated but sub-backlog growth slowed to 6.1%. UBS maintains Neutral at $200 (10x CY28E EV/FCF); Citi cut PT to $188; JPM cut PT to $215; Wolfe cut PT to $175; multiple bear theses cite subscription deceleration for 13 straight quarters. WDAY total RPO grew just 6.1% to $27.5B, $1.1B below Street.

bullets.title: MU: BNP Paribas Exane downgrades to Neutral ($775 PT) amid DRAM/NAND pricing concerns; 2027 oversupply risk rising
bullets.body: BNP Paribas Exane cut MU to Neutral from Outperform with a $775 PT (10% upside from ~$708). MS DRAM outlook: TrendForce cut 1Q27 DRAM price forecast to +3-8% QoQ from prior +5-10%; 2027 NAND bit supply growth 29% vs 19% demand growth, implying surplus and 20-25% ASP declines in 4Q27. HBM demand still strong at 80% YoY bit growth in 2027. Chinese CSPs cutting 2027 server DRAM bit demand outside LTAs in 4Q26; North American CSPs absorbing supply. 2028 broad conventional DRAM price decline risk.

bullets.title: DIS: Wins TRO halting FCC ABC license review; 52-week high; stock +22.9% YTD
bullets.body: Disney secured a temporary restraining order stopping the FCC from continuing its early review of ABC broadcast-station licenses, following an August First Amendment lawsuit claiming retaliatory FCC investigation. DIS also raised its cash dividend by 33% to $2.00/share during the week. DIS hit a 52-week high at $127.00, +22.9% YTD. Coherent authorized a $2B buyback during the same week (DIS and OMC were among the tracked 52-week highs).

bullets.title: AMZN: Acquires Decart for ~$7.5B to boost AWS AI model optimization; BFCM ~52% online share; Muse deal discussions ongoing
bullets.body: Amazon confirmed agreement to acquire AI startup Decart's optimization technology stack (DOS), which achieves 80%+ Model FLOPS Utilization on Trainium3 vs. 40-50% industry average; Decart team joining Amazon. Citi reiterates Buy at $350. Separately, META and AMZN are in advanced discussions to reconnect Muse to Amazon's platform after a September blockade, with talks focusing on search results and advertising revenue split. Holiday consumer survey (Citi) shows Amazon as #1 or #2 retailer for holiday spending with 52% of holiday spend expected online.

bullets.title: TSLA/SPCX: Merger negotiations formalized; RBC estimates TSLA holders receptive at ~$480/share; Optimus supply chain index -5% WoW
bullets.body: TSLA and SpaceX appointed five board members to lead merger negotiations and hired financial advisers; potential announcement could come by early 2027 per RBC. RBC estimates Tesla holders could accept ~$480/share (sum-of-parts intrinsic value + ~15% premium); Musk controls ~82% voting power at SpaceX vs ~20% at Tesla, requiring a deal premium. Strategic synergies cited: superintelligence, chip design, Terafab, robotics, and autonomous mobility. Regulatory hurdles include 50%+ shareholder votes and scrutiny over SpaceX's US defense contracts and Tesla's China assets. Separately, Optimus China Value Chain Index fell 5% WoW contrasting with Tesla stock +10% WoW.

bullets.title: NFLX: Wins World Cup bidding war; purchases $380M LA studio; Muse partnership with BBC
bullets.body: Netflix submitted the highest bid for 2030 World Cup US TV rights, ahead of AMZN and Fox/Univision. NFLX also purchased the Radford Studio Center (1.14M sq ft) in LA for $380M—its first owned LA studio lot. The BBC preschool content partnership and NFL Thanksgiving Eve broadcast with U2 halftime show drove NFLX +1.3% on the week despite the broader AI selloff. NFLX also bidding for FIFA World Cup rights more broadly.
